qa.question: Should NTEC capacity change from 60.5 MW to 41.22 MW per turbine?
qa.finding: The EPA notice gives 742 MW from eighteen turbines, each driving a 41.22 MW generator. GEM and the EIA table show 60.5 MW for each of 18 generators, which is 1,089 MW.
qa.recommendation: Change each single unit GEN1 to GEN12 to 41.2 MW and GEN13-18 to 247.3 MW with Capacity Per Engine 41.2, because the permit gives the generator rating and the manual records electrical nameplate. Keep the unit naming as it is, since all 18 turbines are covered.
qa.note: Open the saved EPA notice at https://web.archive.org/web/20260421215236/https://www.epa.gov/publicnotices/ntec-energy-generation-plant. In the Proposed Action section, the paragraph that starts 'This draft permit, if finalized, will authorize' says 'new 742-megawatt (MW) natural gas-fired power plant' and 'Each combustion turbine will drive a 41.22-MW electrical generator'. Eighteen times 41.22 is 741.96 MW. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx lists 60.5 MW nameplate, 37.6 MW summer and 41.4 MW winter for each of GEN1 to GEN18 on the Planned sheet. The 60.5 MW is probably the turbine rating before the generator. The final permit of August 11, 2026 at https://downloads.regulations.gov/EPA-R09-OAR-2024-0028-0155/content.pdf, Table 1 on page 6, gives the same figures: 'Rated Power Output: 41.22 MW Net-Basis' for each General Electric LM-6000 turbine GEN001 to GEN018 and a 'Combined maximum design capacity of 742 MW Net-Basis'.

qa.question: Is the final NTEC permit issued on August 11, 2026 the same project as the draft?
qa.finding: The EPA actions table at the saved copy lists the NTEC Energy Generation Plant docket EPA-R09-OAR-2024-0028 as Issued on 2026/08/11. No construction start was found.
qa.recommendation: Leave the status as pre-construction and add the permit date to Status Detail. Move to construction only when a source reports work under way.
qa.note: Open https://web.archive.org/web/20261104114042/https://www.epa.gov/caa-permitting/r9-caa-permit-actions and find the row 'NTEC Energy Generation Plant'. The final permit at https://downloads.regulations.gov/EPA-R09-OAR-2024-0028-0155/content.pdf, Table 1 on page 6, keeps eighteen turbines at 41.22 MW each, 742 MW in all. Neither the permit nor any news story found reports construction under way.
